title: Canonical benchmark publication-ingestion register for docs, help, About, evaluation packs, and support exports
summary: Binds every consuming surface that mentions a benchmark claim -- documentation, in-product help, the About surface, enterprise evaluation packs, and support exports -- to the one claim publication entry in the shiproom freshness ledger it renders, so each surface points at the same entry and renders its posture, narrowed effective claim, freshness state, downgrade label, and metric refs verbatim instead of cloning benchmark prose. A binding is authorized only when its reproducibility pack publishes to that surface, discloses only export-safe fields, and a narrowed or quarantined claim propagates to every surface in the same release train.

surface_kinds.description: Published documentation pages render a benchmark claim only from the entry the reproducibility pack publishes to docs.
In-product help topics render a benchmark claim only from the entry the reproducibility pack publishes to help.
The in-product About surface is a help-class surface and surfaces only the entries the reproducibility pack publishes to help.
Enterprise evaluation packs render a benchmark claim only from the entry the reproducibility pack publishes to enterprise evaluation.
Support and diagnostics exports render the redaction-safe projection of any entry the reproducibility pack publishes to help, so support can explain benchmark context without improvising wording.

export_safe_fields.description: The stable claim publication entry id the surface points at.
The strongest claim the entry may make before narrowing.
The entry's narrowed effective claim after freshness and comparability rules apply.
The entry's computed freshness and comparability state.
The entry's reviewable downgrade label explaining its current state.
The protected metric ids the entry covers.
The corpus-manifest revision the entry binds to.
The reference hardware class the entry binds to.
The reference hardware profile id the entry binds to; the raw machine label is withheld.
The lab-image id the entry binds to.
The lab-image revision the entry binds to.
The protected-metrics threshold version the entry binds to.
The reproducibility pack id a reviewer reruns or audits the claim against.

forbidden_fields.why: Raw benchmark run logs stay in retained run metadata and never cross into a product or export surface.
The captured machine's raw hostname or serial is withheld; only the reference hardware profile id is published.
Raw provider request or response bodies never appear in a benchmark surface.
Raw corpus file contents stay in the corpus store and never appear in a published claim.
Customer or repository names drawn from a corpus are never published.
A head-to-head competitor's raw capture payload is withheld; only the disclosed comparison fields are published.
Credentials, tokens, and other secret material never appear in any surface.
Screenshots of a run are not part of an export-safe benchmark projection.

propagation_projection.rationale: No claim-bearing entry's effective claim is below its published ceiling, so docs, help, About, the evaluation pack, and support exports all render the entries' current claims; the quarantined first-paint entry renders as quarantined on every consuming surface.

inspection.how_to_recompute: For each binding, resolve the consumed entry in the freshness ledger and the reproducibility pack in the public-comparison register, then assert the binding's posture, effective claim, freshness state, downgrade label, and metric refs equal the entry's, the reproducibility pack publishes to the binding's surface, and the disclosed fields are export-safe.
inspection.surface_authorization: A binding to a surface is authorized only when its reproducibility pack lists the surface that surface kind requires; the enterprise-evaluation surface authorizes only the head-to-head entry.
inspection.propagation_rule: Every consuming surface renders the entry's narrowed effective claim, not its ceiling, so a narrowing or quarantine in the ledger downgrades docs, help, About, evaluation packs, and support exports in the same release train.
